q: How does a bus operator calculate emissions per passenger-km?
title: Bus operator emissions per passenger-km
short: Multiply the diesel bought for the fleet by 2.68 kg CO2 per litre and divide by passenger-km: passengers carried times km per trip, from tickets or seat logs. Occupancy decides the result, so report per bus-km as well.
audience: Private bus operators and staff transport contractors

ul: Diesel from fuel invoices or fuel cards.
Passengers per trip, from tickets or headcounts.
Trip distance from the route schedule or GPS.

p: Per bus-km shows fuel efficiency; per passenger-km shows how well buses are filled. Clients and schools want the second.
A company hiring your buses for staff reports them in Scope 3, Category 7. A per passenger-km figure from real diesel is better than a default factor.

example.title: Worked example: bus fleet (one month, illustrative inputs)
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use fuel records and ticket counts.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and fuel card statements (diesel 2.68 and CNG 2.69 kg CO2, IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 record. Hired transport goes to the Scope 3 evidence trail, and distance or tonne-km estimates are labelled as estimates.
